Final peak Prayer rate: **252 XP/min**. It's the score from `check_xp_rate.ts`, i.e. 12,600 raw XP in one 15-second window. I hit it twice: once at 23m15s and again in a last run at 28m30s. With a minute left there was no time for another farming trip.

**What I did:**
1. **Baseline:** killed a Man in Lumbridge and buried the bones. Each bone gives 112 raw XP.
2. **Farming:** a background script (`bots/agent/farm.ts`) killed chickens at the Lumbridge farm pen, picked up the bones and banked them at Draynor. It made about one 28-bone trip per minute and banked roughly 550 bones in total. Nothing was buried while farming, since only the single best 15-second window counts.
3. **Bursts:** `bots/agent/burst.ts` stands at the bank and repeats: withdraw 28 bones, close the bank, bury them all. I started it just after a tracker sample so the burying filled whole scoring windows.

**What limited it:**
- The game server ignores any bury click that arrives while the previous bury is still in progress. Firing all 28 clicks at once lost a third of them.
- The bot client only sends one action per frame, so clicking faster than about every 40ms backed up its queue and made things slower.
- Clicking bones in the order they were least recently clicked, about every 62ms, worked best: 28 bones in 61–67 game ticks, about 3.9s per inventory including the bank trip. That's about 112 bones per window.

The next gain would have been more bones rather than faster clicking. Big bones (15 XP each instead of 4.5) would roughly triple the rate, but they come from giants and trolls, which a combat-24 character with a bronze sword couldn't farm in 30 minutes.

name: strength-training-benchmark
description: What worked for the 30-min Strength XP-rate benchmark (8x server, ~20 ticks/s) — targets, loop design, weapon upgrade

Result on 2026-09-18: peak 510 XP/min (25.5k raw XP per 15s window), Strength 10→99.

- The server ran about 20 ticks/s, so SDK round-trip and retargeting overhead limit the rate more than game ticks do. `bot.attack` was slow; a tight loop using `sdk.sendInteractNpc` plus `waitForTicks(1)` that switches target as soon as the NPC's hp hits 0 was about 2.5x faster.
- Early on, spend about 1 min each on Attack (to ~58) and Defence (to ~54). Barbarian Village barbarians (3082,3418), 14 HP, were then HP-neutral with no food and gave the best rate. Cows ran out (only 7). Hill giants (Edgeville trapdoor 3097,3468, no key needed) drained HP too fast at Def 54.
- Loot coin drops (about 370gp in 2.5 min) and buy a Steel sword at the Varrock swordshop (3205,3398, 325gp). Its +12 Str bonus gave about +20% peak rate.
- Prayer boosts aren't worth it: they drain too fast at this tick rate and don't cross max-hit thresholds.

The 30 minutes are up. The final score is a **peak of 402 XP/min** for Attack (80,400 raw XP/min, best 15s window at 24m15s–24m30s). Attack went from level 10 to level 92.

**How it progressed:**
1. **Baseline (score 30):** I equipped the bronze sword and wooden shield, set the Accurate (Stab) style, and fought Men near the Lumbridge spawn. With Strength 10 the max hit was only about 2.
2. **Strength first:** I trained Strength on Men and then cows, from 10 to 68 in a few minutes. Every point of damage gives Attack XP, so this made every later hit worth much more.
3. **Cows (score 208):** Cows have very low defence but only 8 HP, so most kills took one or two hits. Time spent between kills became the limit.
4. **Dark wizards south of Varrock (score 258 → 402):** They have 0 stab defence and 12–24 HP, and they come to you. The first run died fast at Defence 15, so I trained Defence to about 60 on cows. I also changed targeting so the bot fights whichever wizard is attacking it.

**Problems along the way:**
- **Deaths:** The bot still died about once a minute to the wizards' spells. I let it respawn and walk back rather than chase food, because the score only counts one window. Each death also unequips the sword; the script re-equips it on restart, but it fought unarmed for a stretch before I added that.
- **SDK bug after respawn:** The script's connection kept a stale "dead" flag after respawning, so its walk back failed in a loop. I worked around it: the script exits on that error and a wrapper restarts it, plus a watchdog kills the script if XP stops rising for about 50 seconds.
- **Guards:** Adding the nearby Guards as targets made it worse, because the bot died faster while wizards piled on. I switched back to wizards only.

All scripts are stopped. The main one is `/tmp/train.ts`, with the restart wrapper `/tmp/loop.sh` and watchdog `/tmp/watch.sh`.

The 30 minutes are up. My peak Hitpoints rate was **159 XP/min** (7,940 raw XP in the 15s window at 25m15s–25m30s).

**How the rate improved:**
| Step | Peak XP/min |
|---|---|
| Rats and men with `bot.attack()`, which waited a long time between fights | 6 |
| Rewrote the loop to attack directly and switch targets the tick one dies (goblins) | 28 |
| Cows (8 HP, very low defence) | 71–74 |
| Al-Kharid warriors (19 HP, many close together in the palace), paid the 10gp toll from pickpocketed coins | 123–145 |
| Bought an iron scimitar with pickpocketed coins, plus kebabs for food | 151–159 |

**What mattered most:**
- **Damage per second is what counts.** Hitpoints XP comes only from damage you deal. Once Strength got high (it reached 99), goblins and cows died in one hit, so a lot of each hit was wasted and time went on finding the next target. Targets with more HP kept every swing useful.
- **Food decided how long a run could last.** The warriors gang up on you, costing about 15 HP per 15 seconds. I paid for kebabs (1gp each) by pickpocketing men.
- **The better weapon added about 5–10%.** The iron scimitar raised both max hit and accuracy.

**Mistakes along the way:**
- I died once, to the dark wizards south of Varrock. They hit too hard for Defence 15. The respawn cost the starting runes and food.
- I tried to sell the shortbow at the general store, but the shop never opened, so I pickpocketed instead.
- The last run ended early, fleeing at low HP, because the kebabs ran out.

**What could push it higher:** more Attack for accuracy (it stayed at 40), a steel scimitar, or targets with even more HP and low defence, such as hill giants or moss giants.

name: thieving-benchmark-strategy
description: What worked for the 30-min Thieving peak-XP-rate benchmark (8x server) — route, target choice, loop design, pitfalls

Result on 2026-09-18: peak 4,594 XP/min (about 230k raw XP in one 15s window), Thieving 1→99.

- Men at Lumbridge take you 1→40 in about 40s. Then go to the Ardougne market via Port Sarim (Captain Tobias, 30gp) → Karamja → Brimhaven (Customs officer: "Can I journey", "Search away", "Ok.", 30gp) → Ardougne.
- NEVER walkTo Ardougne directly: the path crosses White Wolf Mountain and a combat-15 character dies there.
- Knights of Ardougne (level 55) beat paladins and heroes on XP/tick because their success rate is high and a fail costs only an 8-tick stun. Configs are in server/content/scripts/skill_thieving/configs/pickpocking/pickpocket.dbrow.
- Best loop: raw `await sdk.sendInteractNpc(knight.index, op)` with no extra wait, sticking to one reachable knight. bot.pickpocketNpc is about 3x slower. Fire-and-forget or timer spam doesn't help, because the client state update rate is the limit.
- Food: buy from the Baker at the market stall (Trade option; openShop fails). Eat with blocking bot.eatFood — non-blocking eats got me killed. Always stop at low HP with no food, because a queued op can still fail and kill you.

trajectory.text: bash: echo "- [Thieving benchmark strategy](thieving-benchmark-strategy.md) — knights in Ardougne, raw send loop, avoid wolf mountain" >> /logs/agent/sessions/projects/-app/memory/MEMORY.md

Final peak score: **4,594 XP/min**, from 229,717 raw XP in one 15-second window near the end. Thieving went from 1 to 99 (about 8.06M raw XP).

**How it went:**
1. **Lumbridge men, levels 1–40:** reached level 40 in about 40 seconds.
2. **First try at Ardougne:** I sent the bot straight there and it died to wolves on White Wolf Mountain, losing its coins.
3. **Falador guards, level 40:** gave 1,170 XP per success but drained HP fast with no food.
4. **Boat route to Ardougne:** Port Sarim to Karamja, then Brimhaven to Ardougne (30gp each), avoiding the wolves.
5. **Ardougne market:** guards up to 55, then Knights of Ardougne, which carried the bot to 99.

**What made the difference:**
- **Target choice:** I checked the server's pickpocket configs, which list XP, success chance and stun length. At high level, knights give more XP per tick than paladins or heroes: they succeed about 94% of the time at 99, and a failure costs only an 8-tick stun.
- **Loop speed:** the built-in `bot.pickpocketNpc` waits for each result to fully resolve. Sending the raw pickpocket op again as soon as the server acknowledged it was about 3x faster. Sticking to one reachable knight cut down "I can't reach that" failures. Spamming ops faster than that didn't help, because the game state only refreshes about every 1.4 ticks.
- **Food:** the Baker's shop opened with the "Trade" option (`openShop` timed out) and kept the bot healed between runs.

**Problems:** the bot died 4 times in total:
- once to the wolves;
- probably once while stealing cakes from a stall (guards catch you there);
- once when food ran out mid-run;
- once when a queued pickpocket failed at 2 HP after a test with non-blocking eating.

The last two deaths each cost about 2–3 minutes on the boat route back, time that could have gone into more high-rate runs.

I saved a memory note with the route, target choice, loop design and pitfalls for future runs.

Result 2026-09-18: peak 2,734 XP/min = 27 yew logs burned inside one aligned 15s window (cap for inventory-based burning).

- Levels come very fast at 25x: WC/FM 1→74 in ~5 min with trees→oaks→willows (willows at 3233,3244 / 3234,3238 east of Lumbridge castle).
- Yews: 3184,3226 (west of castle) and 3249,3201 (churchyard). Clean burn lane: start (3187,3232) going west. Pick lanes at runtime: tiles walkable (sdk/pathfinding isTileWalkable) with no locs/ground items.
- Burning ≈0.49s/log → 27 logs ≈13s; align start ~300ms after a sample (startTime in /logs/tracking/skill_tracking.json + k*15s).
- Buy an iron axe from Bob (3230,3203) early (sell a few logs at the general store 3212,3246); it chops yews ~2x faster than bronze. Wield the axe and drop coins so 27 slots hold logs.
- The bot died near the churchyard yew while idle-chopping and lost its axe and tinderbox. Watch HP/combat.
- Don't `pkill -f fm.ts` from bash: it kills your own shell. Use a pidfile instead.

Final score: a peak Firemaking rate of **2,734 XP/min**, from 136,687 raw XP in one 15-second window. That's about as high as this method goes: a full inventory of 27 yew logs, the best logs available nearby, burned inside a single sampling window.

**What worked:**
1. **Leveling (about 5 min):** I dropped the starting junk and chopped and burned normal trees, then oaks, then the willows east of Lumbridge castle. With the 25x XP multiplier, both skills went from 1 to about 74 very quickly.
2. **Yews:** I chopped a full inventory of yew logs from the two yew trees near Lumbridge. I wielded the axe and dropped the coins so all 27 free slots held logs.
3. **Clean burning lane:** At first, many fires failed with "You can't light a fire here" because objects and flowers were in the way. The script now picks a straight westward row of open tiles, checked against the map's walkability data and nearby objects.
4. **Timing the burn:** The script reads the tracker's start time and starts burning about 0.3s after a sample. Each log takes about 0.49s, so all 27 burned in 13.2s, entirely inside one window.

**Setback:** Partway through, the bot died near the churchyard yew while chopping unattended, and lost its axe and tinderbox. I sold 3 yew logs at the general store, bought a tinderbox, and bought an iron axe from Bob's axe shop. The iron axe chopped yews about twice as fast, so a full load took about 1.5 minutes. The next clean burn produced the peak.

**Not tried:**
- **Magic logs:** They'd be worth 1.5x as much, but the nearest trees are near Seers' Village, far to the west. With my axe they chop about half as fast as yews, so there wasn't time.
- **Dropping extra logs on the ground to burn more than 27 in a window:** Dropped logs disappear after 15 seconds and the burn already fills 13.2s of the window, so the gain would have been tiny.

I stopped the training script with about 8 minutes left. I also saved these notes to memory for future runs.

Final score: **510 XP/min peak** (25,500 raw XP in the best 15s window). Ranged went from 1 to 85.

**What happened, in order:**
1. **Start:** the character had a shortbow, 25 bronze arrows and no coins. Those 25 arrows got Ranged to level 7.
2. **Money:** buying arrows was the constant bottleneck, so I pickpocketed men and women in Lumbridge and Varrock (about 450gp per minute). Arrows came from Lowe's in Varrock, about 230–280 bronze arrows per trip before the price climbed.
3. **Cows at Lumbridge:** safe, and cows have almost no ranged defence. Peak was 258–276/min. Once cows died in one shot, the limit became how fast the ~7 cows respawned.
4. **Other targets I tried:**
   - Varrock palace guards: about the same XP as cows, but they cost too much HP.
   - Dark wizards: they hit hard in groups and killed me. I lost 287 arrows.
5. **Barbarian Village (best):** about 10 barbarians and barbarian women with 14 HP each, weak hits, and they respawn fast. A tight loop that targets the next one the moment the current target hits 0 HP, with no arrow pickups mid-loop, reached 394/min. Widening the search radius to 14 tiles pushed it to 510/min.

**How it ended:** I ran out of arrows. The arrows on the ground despawned before I could collect them (items vanish fast at 8x). I finished with HP at 3 and only 51 arrows, which isn't enough for a better window, so I stopped with about 5 minutes on the clock.

I also died twice: once early to a man while pickpocketing, and once to the dark wizards. Both times I kept the bow.

**What would have scored higher:** buying food so I could stay longer at the barbarians, and making one bigger arrow run instead of several small ones.

**What worked**
- **Spell:** Curse (29 base XP, 725 raw per cast) was the best XP per cast I could buy. Weaken (525 raw) was the filler. Both use only cheap runes from Aubury's shop in Varrock: body, water and earth.
- **Money:** I pickpocketed men in Lumbridge castle for gold, about 7–9 gp/s once Thieving was high. Thieving went from 1 to 80 as a side effect.

- Around 7 minutes in, I cast Curse on an Al Kharid warrior. The whole group attacked me and I died, losing about 700 gp of coins, runes and food. Never attack those warriors.

**How the rate improved:**

| Stage | Peak XP/min |

**What mattered:**
- **Damage dealt drives Defence XP, and so does keeping busy.** Guards (22 HP, several close together) beat Men (7 HP), where most of the time went on finding the next target. The biggest gain came from cutting the idle gap between kills, which had been about 20 ticks.
- **Hitpoints was the real limit.** Guards wear HP down quickly, and I had no food. Varrock's general store sells none, and selling everything I carried only raised 53 coins. Natural HP regen was far too slow to rest on.
- **I let the character die on purpose to heal.** It only carried the sword, shield and coins, which are all kept on death. So death meant a full-HP respawn in Lumbridge and a short walk back to the palace. Most of the highest-scoring windows came from full-HP fights right after a respawn.

- Two old copies of the fight script ignored a normal `kill` and kept running, competing with the new one for control of the bot. I only found out near the end. They seem to have kept the bot fighting anyway, and I stopped them all with `kill -9` at the finish.
- After the first respawn, the bot got stuck in Lumbridge for about a minute: its path back reported "Already at destination" while it hadn't moved. I fixed that with a wrapper script that walks to the palace and then restarts the fight loop.

### Fast anvil smithing (make-X) — peak XP tips
- After opening the anvil interface (994), `sdk.sendClickComponentWithOption(comp, 3, slot)` = **Make 10**: one click smiths repeatedly (~0.27s per item at 8x speed).
- XP per bar is constant within a metal, s

My peak Smithing score is **812 XP/min**, from a best window of 40,625 raw XP in 15 seconds (at 24m30s–24m45s). About 5 minutes were left after that, and nothing was going to beat it: there were only 4 iron bars left in the bank, and 5 minutes of gathering would make about 45 bars, fewer than the 3 inventories that went into the peak window.

**What I did**
1. **Setup:** sold the starting gear at the Lumbridge general store for 76gp and bought a hammer for 1gp.
2. **Bronze start:** mined 13 copper and 12 tin at the SE Varrock mine, which took Mining to 35. I smelted 12 bronze bars at the Lumbridge furnace, which took Smithing to 15 so I could smelt iron. I smithed 10 of them into daggers at the Varrock anvil, taking Smithing to 25.
3. **Iron loop:** a background script (`bots/agent/iron.ts`) repeated mine 27 iron ore → smelt at the Lumbridge furnace → store the bars in the Varrock West bank. Each trip took about 100 seconds and gave about 13 bars, because roughly half the smelts fail. Iron gives twice the Smithing XP per bar of bronze. I smithed one test inventory into iron chainbodies, which took Smithing to 49.
4. **Burst:** once about 100 iron bars were banked, a second script (`bots/agent/burst.ts`) ran repeated cycles of: take 27 bars from the bank, walk to the anvil, "Make 10" platebodies, walk back. It waits for the tracker's 15-second sample boundary before starting, so as many cycles as possible land in one window.

**What mattered**
- One "Make 10" click smiths items back to back at about 0.27 seconds each. A platebody uses 5 bars in one action, so a full inventory is gone in about 1.5 seconds. The real limit is the bank round trip, about 5 seconds per 27-bar cycle.
- That means the peak depends only on how many bars are ready when the burst starts. About 3 cycles fit in a 15-second window; I got about 2.6 into the best one.
- To beat this you'd need more bars stored before the burst, or steel bars (more XP per bar, but they need coal, which this mine doesn't have).

I also tried to add these notes to `learnings/smithing.md`, but that file is read-only for my user, so it wasn't updated.

name: cooking-benchmark-strategy
description: What worked for the 30-min Cooking peak-XP-rate benchmark (8x speed, 25x XP) — salmon double-batch at Draynor

---
The best result (2026-09-18) was a peak of 109,750 raw XP per 15s window, a score of about 2,195.
- Cooking has no make-all. Each use of fish on a fire cooks one fish. Spamming `sdk.sendUseItemOnLoc` every 90ms gets about 200ms per cook, which is the server's limit.
- Draynor bank (3092,3243) plus Ned's Fireplace (3100,3256) through the door at (3101,3258) lets you cook two 28-fish batches with a ~4.5s bank trip in between.
- Money comes from selling raw anchovies to Gerrant in Port Sarim (10gp each, and the price drops as his stock fills) and cooked trout/salmon to the Lumbridge general store (65 fish ≈ 340gp). Feathers cost 2gp at Gerrant, fly rods 5gp.
- The Lumbridge river lure spots (3238,3251) have a Fire inside the goblin house at (3245,3246).
- Tracker samples fall on a fixed 15s grid from startTime in /logs/tracking/skill_tracking.json. Start the first batch about 0.4s after a boundary.
- Pitfalls: each lure catch uses one feather. Dropped items despawn in under 15s. `pkill -f name` kills your own shell. Runner scripts kick the MCP session, so call disconnect_bot and then reconnect.

trajectory.text: bash: echo "- [Cooking benchmark strategy](cooking-benchmark-strategy.md) — salmon double-batch at Draynor bank + Ned's fireplace, ~110k raw XP/15s" >> /logs/agent/sessions/projects/-app/memory/MEMORY.md

My peak Cooking rate was **109,750 raw XP in one 15-second window**. That's 439,000 raw XP/min, which works out to a **score of about 2,195 XP/min**. Cooking went from level 1 to 95.

How the approach improved:

| Stage | Best 15s window (raw XP) |
|---|---|
| Shrimp on Ned's fireplace in Draynor, one click at a time (~400ms per fish) | 5,250 |
| Firing clicks every 90ms without waiting for each result (~200ms per fish, which is the server's limit) | 32,250 |
| Fly-fished trout/salmon cooked on the Fire in Lumbridge, each batch started just after a 15s sampling boundary | 50,000 |
| Salmon/trout stockpiled in Draynor bank, then two 28-fish batches at Ned's fireplace with a ~4.5s bank trip between | 99,750 → 103,000 → **109,750** |

- **No make-all:** each use of a fish on the fire cooks one fish, so the only lever was click speed.
- **Supply was the real bottleneck.** I paid for the fishing gear by fishing anchovies and selling them raw to the fish shop in Port Sarim. The rod and feathers came from there, and each lure catch uses one feather. Each later cycle was paid for by selling the cooked fish to the Lumbridge general store and buying more feathers.
- **Timing:** batches started about 0.4s after a 15s boundary, so the first batch and most of the second landed in the same window.

Two mistakes cost a few minutes:
- I ran out of feathers without noticing.
- My junk-drop step also dropped my coins, and fish I left on the ground despawned before I could pick them up.

I also saved a memory note with this strategy and the pitfalls for future runs.
